To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
social interaction in computer mediated environments is a necessary condition for successful learning.

the following factors may impede social interaction in CSCL: (a) taking for granted that social interaction will occur simply because the environment supports it; (b) ignoring the importance of establishing a social (psychological), as opposed to a technical (functional), space; (c) not recognizing the need for a sense of community to develop before social interaction can occur; and (d) neglecting the need for social interaction to develop before learning can occur.

the success of a group in a computer supported collaborative learning environment depends on the group's ability to establish a social space that is characterized by trust, respect, belonging and group cohesion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and avoiding the pitfalls for social interactions in computer-supported collaborative learning environments.
the social interaction of learners, and with the social spaces in which this interaction occurs.
the question of whether the social interaction in computer mediated learning groups can be enhanced by the use of educational techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

social interaction in computer-supported collaborative learning environments is a complex phenomenon that requires a multidisciplinary approach, including educational, social psychological, and computer sciences.
the social dimension of the learning group is of utmost importance and that the environment is a necessary but insufficient condition for the establishment of social interaction.
social interactions are not always as easy to achieve as it is sometimes assumed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social interaction in collaborative environments can be enhanced through a combination of educational strategies and the use of the social space in the environment.
the pitfalls can be avoided by the instructor, by the participants and by a combination of both.

social interaction should not be taken for granted, that the social dimension should be taken into account in the design and implementation of the learning environments, and that the social dimension of learning should be considered as an integral part of the learning process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social interactions that occur in the virtual world are different than in the physical world.
the social interaction in computer-supported collaborative learning environments is more complicated than the technical aspects of the environment.

the design and implementation of computer supported collaborative learning should be informed by a thorough understanding of the social dynamics of the groups involved, and should take into account the social interactions which are required to develop and maintain a sense of community.
